arguments.prompt:
You are working on a Blazor Web App with Interactive Auto render mode (Server + WebAssembly) at `/tmp/sv-bb135e8883f948489ce2425e35d32dd6/ShipmentTracker`. The solution has two projects:

- `ShipmentTracker` (server project) — has EF Core with SQLite, ASP.NET Identity with Individual accounts
- `ShipmentTracker.Client` (WASM project) — runs in browser

The template is already scaffolded with Identity auth. Now build a logistics shipment tracking app.

## Architecture

Since this uses Auto render mode, components may run on Server OR WebAssembly. Data access must work in both modes:
- Create API endpoints on the server
- Create an `IShipmentService` interface in the Client project  
- Create an `HttpShipmentService` in the Client project that calls the API via HttpClient
- Register HttpClient and the service in both Client `Program.cs` and Server `Program.cs`

## What to create

### 1. Shared Model (in Client project so both can reference it)

Create `ShipmentTracker.Client/Models/Shipment.cs`:
```csharp
namespace ShipmentTracker.Client.Models;

public class Shipment
{
    public int Id { get; set; }
    public string TrackingNumber { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    public string Origin { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    public string Destination { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    public ShipmentStatus Status { get; set; }
    public DateTime CreatedDate { get; set; }
    public DateTime? EstimatedDelivery { get; set; }
    public string CustomerEmail { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    public string Description { get; set; } = string.Empty;
}

public enum ShipmentStatus
{
    Pending,
    PickedUp,
    InTransit,
    OutForDelivery,
    Delivered,
    Cancelled
}
```

### 2. Database Entity and DbContext update

Create `ShipmentTracker/Data/ShipmentEntity.cs` — a server-side EF entity mirroring the shared model.

Update `ApplicationDbContext.cs` to add `DbSet<ShipmentEntity>` and configure it with `OnModelCreating` including seed data (8-10 sample shipments with various statuses, realistic tracking numbers like "SHP-20260001", destinations worldwide).

Update `ApplicationUser.cs` to add a `Role` property (string).

### 3. API Controller

Create `ShipmentTracker/Controllers/ShipmentsController.cs`:
- `GET /api/shipments` — returns all shipments (requires auth, Dispatcher role)
- `GET /api/shipments/track/{trackingNumber}` — returns shipment by tracking number (requires auth)
- `PUT /api/shipments/{id}` — updates shipment status (requires auth, Dispatcher role)
- `POST /api/shipments` — creates new shipment (requires auth, Dispatcher role)

Add `builder.Services.AddControllers();` and `app.MapControllers();` to server Program.cs (add BEFORE `app.MapRazorComponents`).

### 4. Client-side Service

Create `ShipmentTracker.Client/Services/IShipmentService.cs`:
```csharp
namespace ShipmentTracker.Client.Services;

public interface IShipmentService
{
    Task<List<Shipment>> GetAllShipmentsAsync();
    Task<Shipment?> TrackShipmentAsync(string trackingNumber);
    Task<Shipment> UpdateShipmentAsync(Shipment shipment);
    Task<Shipment> CreateShipmentAsync(Shipment shipment);
}
```

Create `ShipmentTracker.Client/Services/HttpShipmentService.cs` implementing the interface using `HttpClient`.

### 5. Service Registration

In `ShipmentTracker.Client/Program.cs`, add:
```csharp
builder.Services.AddHttpClient("ServerAPI", client => 
    client.BaseAddress = new Uri(builder.HostEnvironment.BaseAddress))
    .AddHttpMessageHandler<CookieHandler>();
// Actually, for WASM with cookie auth, use:
builder.Services.AddScoped(sp => new HttpClient { BaseAddress = new Uri(builder.HostEnvironment.BaseAddress) });
builder.Services.AddScoped<IShipmentService, HttpShipmentService>();
```

In `ShipmentTracker/Program.cs`, add the same service registrations (HttpClient with base address + IShipmentService as HttpShipmentService) so Auto mode works when running on Server too. Add them after existing service registrations but before `var app = builder.Build();`. Use `builder.Services.AddHttpClient` and `builder.Services.AddScoped<IShipmentService, HttpShipmentService>()`.

### 6. Pages

**Update Home page** (`ShipmentTracker.Client/Pages/Home.razor`) — make it a landing page for the shipment tracker with a brief welcome and links to Track and Dashboard.

**Create `ShipmentTracker.Client/Pages/TrackShipment.razor`** — route `/track`:
- Text input for tracking number + Search button
- Displays shipment details (status, origin, destination, estimated delivery, description)
- Shows a status badge with color coding
- Requires authentication (`@attribute [Authorize]`)
- Uses `@rendermode InteractiveAuto`

**Create `ShipmentTracker.Client/Pages/DispatcherDashboard.razor`** — route `/dashboard`:
- Table of all shipments with columns: Tracking#, Origin, Destination, Status, Customer, Est. Delivery
- Filter dropdown by status
- Button to update status (dropdown + save)  
- Button to create new shipment (inline form or modal)
- Requires Dispatcher role: `@attribute [Authorize(Roles = "Dispatcher")]`
- Uses `@rendermode InteractiveAuto`

### 7. Navigation Update

Update `ShipmentTracker/Components/Layout/NavMenu.razor`:
- Replace Counter and Weather links with:
  - "Track Shipment" → `/track` (visible to all authenticated users)
  - "Dashboard" → `/dashboard` (visible inside `<AuthorizeView Roles="Dispatcher">`)
- Remove the "Auth Required" link
- Keep Home link
- Keep login/logout/register

### 8. Seed Data & Migration

Create a data seeding section in `Program.cs` that:
- Ensures database is created/migrated
- Seeds a Dispatcher user (email: dispatcher@shipments.local, password: Dispatch1!) with confirmed email
- Seeds roles using RoleManager
- Assigns the Dispatcher role to the user
- Seeds sample shipments if none exist

Add role support: add `builder.Services.AddIdentityCore<ApplicationUser>` should also `.AddRoles<IdentityRole>()`.

Create a new EF migration after updating the DbContext.

### 9. Clean up template files

Delete the Counter and Weather pages (both server and client side).
Remove `ShipmentTracker/Components/Pages/` directory contents related to Counter and Weather if they exist.

### Important implementation notes

- The `ShipmentEntity` on the server maps to/from the shared `Shipment` DTO model
- Use `net11.0` target framework (already set)
- The API controller should map between `ShipmentEntity` and `Shipment` model
- Make sure to add proper `@using` statements for models and services in `_Imports.razor` files
- Ensure the build succeeds after all changes

Do the work. Create all files, make all edits, run `dotnet ef migrations add AddShipments` from the server project directory, then run `dotnet build` on the solution to verify everything compiles.

Everything is in great shape. The app builds cleanly and all components are wired up. Here's a summary:

## Shipment Tracker — Built ✅

**Architecture:** Blazor Web App with **Interactive Auto** render mode — Server-side rendering on first visit (fast load), then WebAssembly takes over (no server round-trips).

**Key components:**

| Layer | Files |
|-------|-------|
| **Shared model** | `Client/Models/Shipment.cs` — DTO + `ShipmentStatus` enum |
| **API** | `Controllers/ShipmentsController.cs` — REST endpoints with role-based auth |
| **Service** | `Client/Services/IShipmentService.cs` + `HttpShipmentService.cs` |
| **Pages** | `TrackShipment.razor` (customer tracking) · `DispatcherDashboard.razor` (CRUD + filtering) |
| **Data** | `ShipmentEntity.cs` + EF Core migration + 10 seeded shipments |

**Auth & roles:**
- Individual accounts via ASP.NET Identity (SQLite)
- Seeded dispatcher: `dispatcher@shipments.local` / `Dispatch1!`
- Dashboard restricted to `Dispatcher` role; tracking requires any authenticated user

**Nav** shows Track Shipment for all logged-in users, Dashboard only for Dispatchers.
